response.title: which home battery backup gives the most hours of power for the money without solar
response.answer:
For a home battery backup without solar panels, the best value is usually a large LiFePO₄ (LFP) battery system, rather than a traditional whole-home battery installation.

The key is to compare cost per usable kilowatt-hour (kWh), not just advertised backup hours. A battery that costs half as much per kWh will generally provide about twice as many hours of backup for the same money, assuming similar efficiency.

There are three categories worth comparing:

Expandable portable power stations: EcoFlow, Anker SOLIX, Bluetti. Best for backing up refrigerators, internet, lights, and selected appliances.

Whole-home batteries: Tesla Powerwall, EG4, FranklinWH. Better for automatic backup of household circuits, but installation adds substantial cost.

DIY or professionally assembled LFP battery banks: Often the lowest battery cost per kWh, particularly for larger capacities, but require compatible inverters and appropriate electrical protection.

Based on November 2026 pricing, these are the strongest candidates.

The EG4 price is for the battery alone, so its apparent advantage shrinks once the inverter and installation are included. Still, it is particularly attractive for a larger permanent system.

How many hours will you actually get?

Estimates for one full charge, not guaranteed runtime. High startup loads, inverter standby consumption, and battery operating limits can change results.

Important: Without solar, these batteries only provide power until their stored energy runs out. They recharge from the grid when electricity returns. For outages lasting several days, a generator or another charging source may be more economical than purchasing enough batteries for the entire outage.

My recommendation

If you're primarily trying to maximize backup hours per dollar, I'd start by getting an installed quote for an EG4 14.3 kWh battery with a compatible inverter and comparing it against an expandable EcoFlow system. Make sure the quote includes the transfer equipment, permits, and labor, not just the battery.

One question will make the recommendation much more precise:
